requirement:
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
rationale:
I judged this from the supplied test source only. I did not request implementation source, and no search was run. The tests cover each obligation in `requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax`.

- **Path syntax and empty selector.**
  - `outline/tests.rs#fn[rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry]` asserts that `resolve("")` returns node 0, the root.
  - The same test resolves `/`-separated paths such as `mod[local]/fn[run]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]/fn[run]`. For each one it checks that the resolved node's `selector` equals the input.
  - `selector.rs#mod[tests]/fn[parses_named_anonymous_and_ordinal_segments]` parses empty and multi-segment selectors. It also rejects malformed ones: `fn`, `fn[run`, `[run]`, `fn[run]#0`, `use@123`, `fn[run]x` and `a//b`.
- **Named segment `kind[name]`.** The same two tests cover it. Examples are `struct[Thing]`, `trait[Trait]/type[Item]` and `extern-crate[core]`. `Segment::base` and `to_string` are asserted to produce `fn[run]` and `impl[a%2Fb/c%20d]`.
- **Anonymous segment `kind@hash`, twelve hex digits of the identity hash.**
  - `outline/tests.rs#fn[anonymous_selectors_use_identity_hashes]` asserts that a `use@` selector has length 4 + 12. It also shows that inserting a new `use` leaves the other selectors resolvable, and that changing one `use` breaks only its own selector.
  - `fn[anonymous_container_selectors_use_identity_hashes_and_survive_descendant_edits]` asserts `pair[items]/item@{identity_hash[..12]}`. It asserts that the identity hash differs from the structural hash. It also asserts that editing a descendant keeps the selector stable and still resolves.
  - The segment test checks that hash digits are normalised to lowercase.
- **`#N` disambiguation.**
  - `fn[rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry]` and `fn[selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates]` assert `fn[repeated]#1` and `#2`. The first also asserts that the bare, ambiguous `fn[repeated]` fails to resolve.
  - `fn[duplicate_names_are_numbered_in_source_order_without_line_numbers]` asserts the ordinals follow source order. Swapping the declarations swaps the ordinals, and the byte offset shows `#1` is the first declaration.
  - `fn[anonymous_selectors_use_identity_hashes]` asserts that two identical `use` statements get `#1` and `#2`.
  - Unique nodes are asserted to carry no ordinal (`plain.ordinal == None`, `struct[Thing]`).
- **`line` exception.** `fn[plain_text_lines_are_interchangeable_anonymous_nodes]` asserts that identical lines produce identical `line@` selectors with no `#N`, and that the selector resolves. It also checks the whitespace-word hashing rule: `two  words` and `two words` give the same selector, but `twowords` does not.
- **Percent-encoding.**
  - `selector.rs#mod[tests]/fn[names_round_trip_through_percent_encoding]` encodes a name containing space, `/`, `[`, `]`, `#`, `@`, `%`, tab, and non-ASCII whitespace (NBSP and the ideographic space). It asserts the exact UTF-8 byte encoding, the round trip through `decode_name`, and rejection of unencoded `/`, bad escapes and raw whitespace.
  - `impl[%5Bu8;%204%5D]` is asserted at the outline level.
- **No line numbers.** The duplicate-names test prepends blank lines. It asserts that the selectors stay identical, while `line_start` changes from 1 to 4.

The cited `requirements.references.structural_hash` is applied where the subject uses it. The tests check the identity hash for anonymous nodes and the word-based line hash. The assessment does not re-judge the structural-hash requirement itself.

I found no unnamed gaps. Rejecting non-hex digits in an anonymous segment is not tested, but the requirement does not state it.

text: :::{req} selector_syntax
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
